# Script to vizualise/plot the phylogenetic trees created with clootl
## configuration
```{r}
library(clootl)
library(ape)
library(phytools)

#2025 database 
taxonomy25 <- clootl_data$taxonomies$year2025
```


## 1. Parrots
```{r}
#1. Parrots


outgroup_species <- "Falco peregrinus" 

parrot_species_out <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[
  (taxonomy25$ORDER == "Psittaciformes") | 
    (taxonomy25$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species)
]

parrot_tree_out <- extractTree(
  species = parrot_species_out, 
  label_type = "scientific", 
  taxonomy_year = 2025
)



#to highlight a few specific species
species_to_keep <- c("Myiopsitta monachus", "Agapornis roseicollis", "Agapornis fischeri") # 

# Create a reference data frame of species and look up their FAMILY
tip_df <- data.frame(SCI_NAME = gsub("_", " ", parrot_tree_out$tip.label))
tip_df$FAMILY <- taxonomy25$FAMILY[match(tip_df$SCI_NAME, taxonomy25$SCI_NAME)]
tip_df$FAMILY[tip_df$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species] <- "Falconidae"

# Create a custom grouping column: Use the species name if it's in your list, 
# otherwise default to the Family name (which now applies to the outgroup too)
tip_df$PLOT_LABEL <- ifelse(
  tip_df$SCI_NAME %in% species_to_keep, 
  tip_df$SCI_NAME, 
  tip_df$FAMILY
)

#identify tips to KEEP and DROP based on your custom PLOT_LABEL
all_tips <- parrot_tree_out$tip.label
kept_tips <- parrot_tree_out$tip.label[!duplicated(tip_df$PLOT_LABEL)]
tips_to_drop <- setdiff(all_tips, kept_tips)

#drop the duplicate tips from the tree structure
parrot_tree_collapsed <- drop.tip(parrot_tree_out, tips_to_drop)

#rename the remaining unique tips to your custom labels
final_labels <- tip_df$PLOT_LABEL[match(gsub("_", " ", parrot_tree_collapsed$tip.label), tip_df$SCI_NAME)]
parrot_tree_collapsed$tip.label <- final_labels

#plot tree
plot(parrot_tree_collapsed, cex = 0.8, no.margin = TRUE)
```

## 2. Threskiornithidae
```{r}
#tree with genera

outgroup_species <- "Gorsachius goisagi" 

thre_species_out <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[
  (taxonomy25$FAMILY == "Threskiornithidae (Ibises and Spoonbills)") | 
    (taxonomy25$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species)
]

thre_tree_out <- extractTree(
  species = thre_species_out, 
  label_type = "scientific", 
  taxonomy_year = 2025
)

#create a reference data frame of species and their corresponding GENUS
tip_df <- data.frame(SCI_NAME = gsub("_", " ", thre_tree_out$tip.label))

#extract the genus (the first word of the scientific name)
tip_df$GENUS <- sapply(strsplit(tip_df$SCI_NAME, " "), `[`, 1)

#ensure the outgroup keeps its unique full name 
tip_df$GENUS[tip_df$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species] <- "family Ardeidae"

#identify which tips to KEEP (only the first species representing each genus)
#identify which tips to DROP (all duplicate species within the same genus)
all_tips <- thre_tree_out$tip.label
kept_tips <- thre_tree_out$tip.label[!duplicated(tip_df$GENUS)]
tips_to_drop <- setdiff(all_tips, kept_tips)

#drop the duplicate tips from the tree structure
thre_tree_collapsed <- drop.tip(thre_tree_out, tips_to_drop)

#rename the remaining unique tips to their Genus names
final_genera <- tip_df$GENUS[match(gsub("_", " ", thre_tree_collapsed$tip.label), tip_df$SCI_NAME)]
thre_tree_collapsed$tip.label <- final_genera

#plot tree

plot(thre_tree_collapsed, cex = 1.5, no.margin = TRUE)


#tree with the families within pelecaniformes

pelecaniformes_families <- c(
  "Threskiornithidae (Ibises and Spoonbills)",
  "Ardeidae (Herons, Egrets, and Bitterns)",
  "Scopidae (Hamerkop)",
  "Balaenicipitidae (Shoebill)",
  "Pelecanidae (Pelicans)"
)

pelecaniformes_species <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[taxonomy25$FAMILY %in% pelecaniformes_families]

outgroup_species <- "Sula sula" 
pelecaniformes_species_out <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[
  (taxonomy25$FAMILY %in% pelecaniformes_families) | 
    (taxonomy25$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species)
]

# 2. Extract the full species-level tree
pelecaniformes_tree_out <- extractTree(
  species = pelecaniformes_species_out, 
  label_type = "scientific", 
  taxonomy_year = 2025
)

pelecaniformes_tree_out <- root(pelecaniformes_tree_out, outgroup = outgroup_species, resolve.root = TRUE)


#create a reference data frame of species and their corresponding family
tip_df <- data.frame(SCI_NAME = gsub("_", " ", pelecaniformes_tree_out$tip.label))
tip_df$FAMILY <- taxonomy25$FAMILY[match(tip_df$SCI_NAME, taxonomy25$SCI_NAME)]
# Ensure the outgroup keeps its unique name
tip_df$FAMILY[tip_df$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species] <- "Suliformes"

#identify which tips to KEEP (only the first species representing each family)
kept_tips_df <- tip_df[!duplicated(tip_df$FAMILY), ]

#identify which tips to DROP (all the duplicate species in those families)
all_tips <- pelecaniformes_tree_out$tip.label
kept_tips <- pelecaniformes_tree_out$tip.label[!duplicated(tip_df$FAMILY)]
tips_to_drop <- setdiff(all_tips, kept_tips)

#drop the duplicate tips from the tree structure
pelecaniformes_tree_collapsed <- drop.tip(pelecaniformes_tree_out, tips_to_drop)

#rename the remaining unique tips to their Family names
final_families <- tip_df$FAMILY[match(gsub("_", " ", pelecaniformes_tree_collapsed$tip.label), tip_df$SCI_NAME)]
pelecaniformes_tree_collapsed$tip.label <- final_families

#plot tree
plot(pelecaniformes_tree_collapsed, cex = 1.3, no.margin = TRUE)
```

## 3. Sylviida
```{r}
sylviida_families <- c(
  "Alaudidae (Larks)",       
  "Hirundinidae (Swallows)",    
  "Cettiidae (Bush Warblers and Allies)",       
  "Phylloscopidae (Leaf Warblers)",  
  "Acrocephalidae (Reed Warblers and Allies)",   
  "Locustellidae (Grassbirds and Allies)",   
  "Cisticolidae (Cisticolas and Allies)",    
  "Macrosphenidae (African Warblers)",  
  "Pycnonotidae (Bulbuls)",    
  "Sylviidae (Sylviid Warblers and Allies)",      
  "Paradoxornithidae (Parrotbills)",
  "Zosteropidae (White-eyes, Yuhinas, and Allies)",    
  "Timaliidae (Tree-Babblers, Scimitar-Babblers, and Allies)",       
  "Pellorneidae (Ground Babblers and Allies)",    
  "Leiothrichidae (Laughingthrushes and Allies)" ,
  "Panuridae (Bearded Reedling)",
  "Timaliidae (Tree-Babblers, Scimitar-Babblers, and Allies)",
  "Nicatoridae (Nicators)"
)

sylviida_species <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[taxonomy25$FAMILY %in% sylviida_families]

outgroup_species <- "Taeniopygia guttata" 
sylviida_species_out <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[
  (taxonomy25$FAMILY %in% sylviida_families) | 
    (taxonomy25$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species)
]

# 2. Extract the full species-level tree
sylviida_tree_out <- extractTree(
  species = sylviida_species_out, 
  label_type = "scientific", 
  taxonomy_year = 2025
)


#create a reference data frame of species and their corresponding family
tip_df <- data.frame(SCI_NAME = gsub("_", " ", sylviida_tree_out$tip.label))
tip_df$FAMILY <- taxonomy25$FAMILY[match(tip_df$SCI_NAME, taxonomy25$SCI_NAME)]
# Ensure the outgroup keeps its unique name
tip_df$FAMILY[tip_df$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species] <- "Taeniopygia guttata (non-Sylvioidea passerine)"

#identify which tips to KEEP (only the first species representing each family)
kept_tips_df <- tip_df[!duplicated(tip_df$FAMILY), ]

#identify which tips to DROP (all the duplicate species in those families)
all_tips <- sylviida_tree_out$tip.label
kept_tips <- sylviida_tree_out$tip.label[!duplicated(tip_df$FAMILY)]
tips_to_drop <- setdiff(all_tips, kept_tips)

#drop the duplicate tips from the tree structure
sylviida_tree_collapsed <- drop.tip(sylviida_tree_out, tips_to_drop)

#rename the remaining unique tips to their Family names
final_families <- tip_df$FAMILY[match(gsub("_", " ", sylviida_tree_collapsed$tip.label), tip_df$SCI_NAME)]
sylviida_tree_collapsed$tip.label <- final_families

#plot tree
plot(sylviida_tree_collapsed, cex = 1, no.margin = TRUE)

#only the species with additional neo-sex fusion

sylviida_families_reduced <- c(
  "Alaudidae (Larks)",
  "Panuridae (Bearded Reedling)",
  "Nicatoridae (Nicators)",
  "Macrosphenidae (African Warblers)",
  "Cisticolidae (Cisticolas and Allies)",
  "Locustellidae (Grassbirds and Allies)"
  
)

sylviida_species_reduced <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[taxonomy25$FAMILY %in% sylviida_families_reduced]

outgroup_species <- "Taeniopygia guttata" 
sylviida_species_out <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[
  (taxonomy25$FAMILY %in% sylviida_families_reduced) | 
    (taxonomy25$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species)
]

# 2. Extract the full species-level tree
sylviida_tree_out <- extractTree(
  species = sylviida_species_out, 
  label_type = "scientific", 
  taxonomy_year = 2025
)

# Root the tree
sylviida_tree_out <- root(sylviida_tree_out, outgroup = outgroup_species, resolve.root = TRUE)

#create a reference data frame of species and their corresponding family
tip_df <- data.frame(SCI_NAME = gsub("_", " ", sylviida_tree_out$tip.label))
tip_df$FAMILY <- taxonomy25$FAMILY[match(tip_df$SCI_NAME, taxonomy25$SCI_NAME)]
# Ensure the outgroup keeps its unique name
tip_df$FAMILY[tip_df$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species] <- "Taeniopygia guttata (non-Sylvioidea passerine)"


#identify which tips to KEEP (only the first species representing each family)
kept_tips_df <- tip_df[!duplicated(tip_df$FAMILY), ]

#identify which tips to DROP (all the duplicate species in those families)
all_tips <- sylviida_tree_out$tip.label
kept_tips <- sylviida_tree_out$tip.label[!duplicated(tip_df$FAMILY)]
tips_to_drop <- setdiff(all_tips, kept_tips)

#drop the duplicate tips from the tree structure
sylviida_tree_collapsed <- drop.tip(sylviida_tree_out, tips_to_drop)

#rename the remaining unique tips to their Family names
final_families <- tip_df$FAMILY[match(gsub("_", " ", sylviida_tree_collapsed$tip.label), tip_df$SCI_NAME)]
final_families[final_families == "Locustellidae (Grassbirds and Allies)"] <- "Other Sylvioidea passerines"
sylviida_tree_collapsed$tip.label <- final_families

#plot tree
plot(sylviida_tree_collapsed, cex = 0.8, no.margin = TRUE)
```

## 4. Meliphagidae
```{r}
#for Meliphagiade I only want the clade in which neo-sex fusions have been identified


outgroup_species <- "Taeniopygia guttata" 

#all species for the Meliphagidae family + your outgroup
mel_species_out <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[
  (taxonomy25$FAMILY == "Meliphagidae (Honeyeaters)") | 
    (taxonomy25$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species)
]

#extract the full species-level tree
mel_tree_out <- extractTree(
  species = mel_species_out, 
  label_type = "scientific", 
  taxonomy_year = 2025
)


#create a reference data frame of species and their corresponding GENUS
tip_df <- data.frame(SCI_NAME = gsub("_", " ", mel_tree_out$tip.label))

#extract the genus (the first word of the scientific name)
tip_df$GENUS <- sapply(strsplit(tip_df$SCI_NAME, " "), `[`, 1)

#ensure the outgroup keeps its unique full name so it doesn't just display "Taeniopygia"
tip_df$GENUS[tip_df$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species] <- "Taeniopygia guttata (outgroup)"

#identify which tips to KEEP (only the first species representing each genus)
#identify which tips to DROP (all duplicate species within the same genus)
all_tips <- mel_tree_out$tip.label
kept_tips <- mel_tree_out$tip.label[!duplicated(tip_df$GENUS)]
tips_to_drop <- setdiff(all_tips, kept_tips)

#drop the duplicate tips from the tree structure
mel_tree_collapsed <- drop.tip(mel_tree_out, tips_to_drop)

#rename the remaining unique tips to their Genus names
final_genera <- tip_df$GENUS[match(gsub("_", " ", mel_tree_collapsed$tip.label), tip_df$SCI_NAME)]
mel_tree_collapsed$tip.label <- final_genera

#plot complete tree

plot(mel_tree_collapsed, cex = 0.6, no.margin = TRUE)



# --- reduced tree ---

#genera I want to keep 
genera_to_keep <- c("Ptiloprora", "Melipotes", "Conopophila", "Melilestes", "Phylidonyris", "Entomyzon", "Nesoptilotis", "Manorina", "Lichenostomus","Philemon", "Myzomela", "Acanthiza", "Pardalotus") 

genera_to_keep <- c("Ptiloprora", "Melipotes", "Conopophila",  "Entomyzon", "Manorina", "Lichenostomus","Philemon", "Myzomela", "Acanthiza", "Pardalotu","Phylidonyris")

#include the outgroup label in your allowed list so it doesn't get dropped
allowed_labels <- c(genera_to_keep, "Taeniopygia guttata (outgroup)")
# --------------------------------------------

#identify tips to KEEP (Only the first representative of our CHOSEN genera)
kept_tips <- mel_tree_out$tip.label[
  !duplicated(tip_df$GENUS) & (tip_df$GENUS %in% allowed_labels)
]

#indentify ALL tips to DROP (Everything else in the tree)
all_tips <- mel_tree_out$tip.label
tips_to_drop <- setdiff(all_tips, kept_tips)

#dop the unwanted tips
mel_tree_collapsed <- drop.tip(mel_tree_out, tips_to_drop)

#rename the remaining unique tips to their Genus names
final_genera <- tip_df$GENUS[match(gsub("_", " ", mel_tree_collapsed$tip.label), tip_df$SCI_NAME)]
mel_tree_collapsed$tip.label <- final_genera

#plot subset tree
plot(mel_tree_collapsed, cex = 1.5, no.margin = TRUE)
```

##7. Passerines tree
```{r}
#Passerines tree
outgroup_species <- "Myiopsitta monachus" 
target_families <- c("Alaudidae (Larks)","Panuridae (Bearded Reedling)","Nicatoridae (Nicators)","Macrosphenidae (African Warblers)", "Cisticolidae (Cisticolas and Allies)",
 "Locustellidae (Grassbirds and Allies)","Sturnidae (Starlings)", "Meliphagidae (Honeyeaters)", "Petroicidae (Australasian Robins)", "Pipridae (Manakins)" )  # Add your target family/families here
other_species <-"Locustellidae (Grassbirds and Allies)"

pas_species_out <- taxonomy25$SCI_NAME[
  ((taxonomy25$ORDER == "Passeriformes") & (taxonomy25$FAMILY %in% target_families)) | 
    (taxonomy25$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species)
]

pas_tree_out <- extractTree(
  species = pas_species_out, 
  label_type = "scientific", 
  taxonomy_year = 2025
)

#create a reference data frame matching tree tips to their FAMILY
tip_df <- data.frame(SCI_NAME = gsub("_", " ", pas_tree_out$tip.label))
tip_df$FAMILY <- taxonomy25$FAMILY[match(tip_df$SCI_NAME, taxonomy25$SCI_NAME)]

#ensure the outgroup keeps its label instead of displaying NA or non-passerine family
tip_df$FAMILY[tip_df$SCI_NAME == outgroup_species] <- "Non-passerines"
tip_df$FAMILY[tip_df$FAMILY == other_species] <- "Other Sylvioidea passerines"



all_tips <- pas_tree_out$tip.label
kept_tips <- pas_tree_out$tip.label[!duplicated(tip_df$FAMILY)]
tips_to_drop <- setdiff(all_tips, kept_tips)

#drop duplicate tips from the tree structure so only one representative per family remains
pas_tree_collapsed <- drop.tip(pas_tree_out, tips_to_drop)

#rename the remaining tips to their Family names
final_families <- tip_df$FAMILY[match(gsub("_", " ", pas_tree_collapsed$tip.label), tip_df$SCI_NAME)]
pas_tree_collapsed$tip.label <- final_families

#plot complete tree

plot(pas_tree_collapsed, cex = 1.2, no.margin = TRUE)
```

## 8. Avian neo sex fusion tree not including my new species 
```{r}
species_to_keep <- c( "Pluvialis apricaria", "Panurus biarmicus", "Alauda arvensis","Cisticola juncidis", "Nicator vireo", "Sylvietta brachyura", "Entomyzon cyanotis", "Myiopsitta monachus", "Melopsittacus undulatus", "Nipponia nippon", "Sula sula", "Harpia harpyja", "Crotophaga ani", "Eopsaltria australis", "Pavo cristatus", "Anser cygnoides", "Anas acuta", "Aythya fuligula", "Chlamydotis macqueenii", "Balearica regulorum", "Myzomela cardinalis", "Philemon citreogularis", "Sula granti", "Sula dactylatra", "Amazona aestiva", "Agapornis roseicollis", "Agapornis fischeri", "Guira guira", "Pygoscelis adeliae", "Gulosus aristotelis", "Calonectris diomedea", "Spheniscus humboldti", "Nyctibius grandis", "Podargus strigoides", "Calypte anna", "Archilochus colubris", "Colius striatus", "Dryobates pubescens", "Pogoniulus pusillus", "Pseudopipra pipra", "Poecile atricapillus", "Eopsaltria australis")

avian_tree <- extractTree(
  species = species_to_keep, 
  label_type = "scientific", 
  taxonomy_year = 2025,
  force = TRUE
)

# 3. Plotagem da árvore
plot(avian_tree, cex = 1.5, no.margin = TRUE)



#changing the fonts
# Set global font parameter to 3 (Italic) and family to serif
par(font = 3, family = "sans") 

# Plot your tree
tree_plot <- plot(avian_tree, cex = 1, no.margin = TRUE)


#coloring specific clades
library(ggtree)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Build and store the complete ggtree object into a variable
final_tree <- ggtree(avian_tree, linewidth = 0.5, color = "black") + 
  
  # Highlight terminal branches for target species
  geom_tree(data = function(df) {
    df %>% filter(isTip & label %in% c(
      "Platalea leucorodia", "Acridotheres tristis", 
      "Theristicus caerulescens", "Caloenas nicobarica", 
      "Leptosomus discolor", "Pterocles gutturalis"
    ))
  }, aes(color = label), linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Format tip labels
  geom_tiplab(aes(color = label), size = 6, fontface = "italic") +
  
  # Map custom colors
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Platalea leucorodia"     = "red",
      "Theristicus caerulescens" = "red",
      "Acridotheres tristis"     = "red",
      "Caloenas nicobarica"     = "red",
      "Leptosomus discolor"     = "red",
      "Pterocles gutturalis"    = "red"
    ),
    na.value = "black" # Keeps non-target species black
  ) +
  
  # Expand x-axis limit so long tip names don't get cut off
  xlim(0, max(node.depth.edgelength(avian_tree)) * 1.5) +
  
  # Remove legend and force crisp white background
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# 2. Save using the correct plot object variable ('final_tree')
ggsave(
  filename = "avian_tree_large_new.png", 
  plot = final_tree, 
  width = 10, 
  height = 18, 
  units = "in", 
  dpi = 300, 
  bg = "white"
)


# 1. Open the PNG graphics device FIRST
png("avian_tree_large_new.png", width = 10, height = 18, units = "in", res = 300)

# 2. Set font parameters inside the active PNG device
# (font = 3 is Italic, family = "sans" sets a clean sans-serif font)
par(font = 3, family = "sans")

# 3. Draw the tree directly to the PNG device
plot(avian_tree, cex = 1, no.margin = TRUE)

# 4. Save and close the file
dev.off()
```

tree_plot <- plot(avian_tree, cex = 1, no.margin = TRUE)


#coloring specific clades
library(ggtree)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Build and store the complete ggtree object into a variable
final_tree <- ggtree(avian_tree, linewidth = 0.5, color = "black") + 
  
  # Highlight terminal branches for target species
  geom_tree(data = function(df) {
    df %>% filter(isTip & label %in% c(
      "Platalea leucorodia", "Acridotheres tristis", 
      "Theristicus caerulescens", "Caloenas nicobarica", 
      "Leptosomus discolor", "Pterocles gutturalis"
    ))
  }, aes(color = label), linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Format tip labels
  geom_tiplab(aes(color = label), size = 6, fontface = "italic") +
  
  # Map custom colors
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Platalea leucorodia"     = "red",
      "Theristicus caerulescens" = "red",
      "Acridotheres tristis"     = "red",
      "Caloenas nicobarica"     = "red",
      "Leptosomus discolor"     = "red",
      "Pterocles gutturalis"    = "red"
    ),
    na.value = "black" # Keeps non-target species black
  ) +
  
  # Expand x-axis limit so long tip names don't get cut off
  xlim(0, max(node.depth.edgelength(avian_tree)) * 1.5) +
  
  # Remove legend and force crisp white background
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# 2. Save using the correct plot object variable ('final_tree')
ggsave(
  filename = "avian_tree_large_new.png", 
  plot = final_tree, 
  width = 10, 
  height = 18, 
  units = "in", 
  dpi = 300, 
  bg = "white"
)


# 1. Open the PNG graphics device FIRST
png("avian_tree_large_new.png", width = 10, height = 18, units = "in", res = 300)

# 2. Set font parameters inside the active PNG device
# (font = 3 is Italic, family = "sans" sets a clean sans-serif font)
par(font = 3, family = "sans")

# 3. Draw the tree directly to the PNG device
plot(avian_tree, cex = 1, no.margin = TRUE)

# 4. Save and close the file
dev.off()
